slice: 2 · Profiles, journeys and the change log

requirements.text: Plans can be straight, back-loaded ((w/13)^1.5) or stepped, and set the weekly checkpoint.
Forecast is the last three weeks' slope projected to the end of the cycle, and only shown with enough data.
Changing a plan after check-ins start re-baselines it and keeps the original visible.
Metric: on track at 95% of planned progress or more, at risk 80–95%, off track below 80%.
Lower-is-better metrics are judged the same way as higher-is-better ones.
Range: at risk inside the warning margin or after one breach; off track after two weeks out of range.
Milestone: a stage up to 2 weeks late is at risk, more is off track; an overdue stage counts as late.
The owner's call is the official status shown everywhere, with the calculated status beside it.
A call greener than the calculation needs a reason and is flagged on the goal.
A reason (cause and explanation) is required when behind plan (below 95%).
A reason is required when 120% or more ahead, and the check-in asks whether the target should change.
At risk and Off track need a path to green: what changes and a future week it is back on plan by, plus any decision needed.
The check-in shows actual against plan today, the gap, the forecast and the calculated status as the value is typed.
One check-in per goal per week; editing replaces it.
Only the goal's owner can post its check-in.
No owner check-in for 14 days shows as Stale, never as on track.
A headline goal with input goals from several teams, each with an estimated effect; the headline shows its inputs and their mix of statuses.
A lead can create a metric, range or milestone goal with a plan, and invalid input is explained.
The goal page shows status strip, why, path to green, chart with plan/forecast/path back, and check-in history.
Changes are saved and survive a reload; demo data can be reset.
Every screen works at phone width (390px) with no horizontal scrolling.
No serious or critical accessibility violations (axe-core); status is shape plus word, never colour alone.
No console or page errors on any screen.
Each profile (team lead, sponsor, coach, contributor) gets its own home with one clear next thing to do.
Off track, stale, a worsening trend, a missed or missing path to green, and pending proposals are flagged where the user starts, with the reason in one line.
The sponsor works the review queue to zero, one goal at a time; every call is recorded and an approved target re-baselines the plan.
Every save (goal, plan, check-in, comment, decision, workspace) is logged with who, when and each field's before and after. Drafts are not logged.
Unsaved answers survive leaving a flow and are offered back when the user returns.
The example and your own data live in separate workspaces; you can load your own from a spreadsheet, with every row checked, and switch back.
Motion is subtle and never blocks; it switches off under reduced motion. Loading shows a skeleton, not a blank page.

journeys.title: Weekly check-in, all due goals in one pass
What needs me? Home shows what's due, off track, stale or slipping
Weekly review: work the queue to zero and make the calls
Set up a goal, step by step
Load your own data and switch between it and the example
Understand a goal and its change history
Propose a target change and get it approved
See how my team's work maps to the goals
Close the cycle with a retro

easeCriteria.text: Starts from the person's home, with the way in visible without scrolling
Every step shows exactly one primary action
The person can see how far along they are (ring, steps or count)
Done within the interaction budget for the journey
An incomplete step says what's missing, in place, instead of failing silently
Finishing is confirmed, with the next thing offered
Anything off track, stale or slipping in the journey is flagged with its reason
The same journey completes on a 390px phone and a 1440px desktop
No serious accessibility issues; primary buttons are at least 44px tall on a phone
The change it makes is in the change log with who, when and before → after
